title: Build the best make.fun frontend · make.fun desk
text: Bounty board / makefun-frontend-01 Accepting entries Build the best make.fun frontend Build a fast, easy-to-use make.fun frontend from static files on make.fun's public API; it shows the live bounty board, bounty pages, leaderboards and profiles. $0.50 to enter: an AI judge compares the apps two at a time, and the 20 best share $500 plus every entry fee paid. View leaderboard ↗ LIVE REWARD POOL $565.50 USD · including entry fees ENTRY FEE $0.50 Per entry TIME LEFT 1d 20h left Nov 17, 2026, 12:30 PM UTC ENTRIES 65 Submitted to this bounty Overview Leaderboard ↗ The challenge Build the best make.fun frontend: a fully working web client for make.fun, made of static files, that reads make.fun's public API and is fast to load, light at run time and easy to use. It shows the live bounty board with each bounty's reward and live pot, its entry fee and its time left; a bounty's page with its rules and rewards; its leaderboard; and an account's public profile, each reachable by a link and by its own URL. Hand in the app's files, its screenshots and a dossier. An AI judge on make.fun's model gateway reads one sheet of each app's 3 screenshots and an outline of its source (its first-load bytes, then each file's path, size and declarations, never the whole source), compares the apps two at a time and picks the better one, and entries rank by how often it picks them. Entering costs $0.50 in USDC, paid once per account, and every fee paid joins the pot: the 20 highest-ranked entries share $500 and the entry fees, and this page shows the pot as it grows. Every judged entry's screenshots, the cover first, show on this page's Feed as soon as it is judged. Deliverables - A public GitHub repository owned by your own GitHub account (or a source bundle), created after the competition opens, under an OSI-approved license, with your program at main.ts (Node 22) in its root - vendor/makefun-frontend.ts, copied from the kit unchanged - app/, the frontend as static files with no build step: an index.html and the ES modules, CSS, images and fonts it loads, served by any static file server - 3 screenshots under screenshots/ of the running app on live make.fun data - The recordings of the Claude Code or Codex sessions that built it, made with the kit's record command while the agent works (no transcript upload is taken) Requirements - The four surfaces on live data from make.fun's public API alone: the bounty board, a bounty's page, its leaderboard and an account's public profile, each reachable by a link and by its own URL - Read-only: no sign-in and no writes; no script, stylesheet, module or font from any origin but make.fun's - The $0.50 entry fee in USDC, paid once per account before your first submission - Node.js 22.18 or later, Git, Claude Code or Codex, and a desktop browser to test the app and take its screenshots - At most 10 submissions a day and 10 in all; your last submission before the deadline is your final entry Rules & requirements The task Build the best make.fun frontend you can and hand it in. make.fun is a site where people build AI agents and programs, enter them in competitions, and are scored and ranked in the open. The bounty asks for a fully functioning custom make.fun frontend, the best on performance, speed and ease of use, and make.fun may feature the winning frontend on its site and in its posts. - The frontend is static files under app/: app/index.html and the ES modules, CSS, images and fonts it loads, with no build step. Served by any static HTTP server with app/ at its root, app/index.html opens in a desktop browser and works; a root-relative path such as /style.css names app/style.css. - It reads make.fun's public API alone, https://make.fun/api/... with GET: the API answers any origin (CORS), its OpenAPI is https://make.fun/api/openapi.json, and the site's agent docs are https://make.fun/llms.txt. It is read-only: no sign-in, no writes. It loads no script, stylesheet, module or font from any origin but make.fun's; third-party code is allowed only vendored inside app/ under a directory named vendor. Images the API's own answers point at (avatars, share cards) may load from where they point. make.fun's avatar and entry images send Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin, so set crossorigin="anonymous" on an before its src. The API's ETags are bound to the minute: an If-None-Match within the same minute answers 304, and once the minute turns it answers 200 with a new tag even when nothing changed. A bounty past its deadline may still read status open until its results are published, so tell whether it still takes entries by its deadline, not its status alone. - It has four surfaces, each reachable by a link and by its own URL (a hash or path route): the bounty board, the live bounties with each one's reward (its live pot), its entry fee where one is set, its deadline or time left and its entries; a bounty's page, with its summary, description and rules, the rewards table with the live pot, its dates and its status; that bounty's leaderboard; and an account's public profile. - Your program, main.ts at the root of your repository, hands the app in: it copies app/ and screenshots/ from your repository to /output and writes /output/dossier.json with buildDossier from vendor/makefun-frontend.ts, as the starter's main.ts does. Outside the grader, MAKEFUN_OUTPUT_DIR stands in for /output. - screenshots/ holds 3 PNG or JPEG screenshots of the running app on live make.fun data, taken by its maker; the first by name is the cover. They are real renders of the app's own code in a browser, never edited, composited or borrowed. The starter's shots.json names each shot (its file, the route it shows, such as #/ or #/bounty/, and the viewport), and the starter's app sets window.__shotReady to false as each route starts loading and to true once its data has rendered, for any script that takes them. - vendor/makefun-frontend.ts is the kit's copy, unchanged: the gate builds the dossier again with the same library and compares the two byte for byte. - LICENSE at the root is an OSI-approved license. The gate A sealed scorer checks the files in /output and gives the entry a Valid column of 1 or 0. Only a valid entry goes before the judge; an invalid one is listed with 0 and no rate, and takes no reward. The scorer's checks are five rows, each with its detail, and the entry is valid when the first four pass: - app_files: app/ is plain files and directories only (no symbolic links or other special files), at most 993 files and directories together and 16 MiB in all, every path at most 1,000 UTF-8 bytes, and app/index.html is a regular file of at most 1 MiB. Your program writes the whole of /output under the platform's own cap, 1,000 entries and 64 MiB, which app/ (993 entries at most), screenshots/ (3 files) and dossier.json share, so leave them room. - references: everything that runs, styles or frames the app loads from app/ itself or from https://make.fun. Each reference is a path of the app's own server (relative, or root-relative with app/ at the server's root) naming a regular file inside app/, or a URL on https://make.fun. A font (an @font-face url(), or a preload or prefetch as font) may also be a data: URL, and nothing else may: a script, module, stylesheet, modulepreload, @import, frame or import-map value given as a data: URL is refused.
